function.name: most_frequent_visitor
function.description: Retrieve the visitor who visited the museum the most within a given period. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

start_date.description: The start date of the period, format: yyyy-mm-dd.

end_date.description: The end date of the period, format: yyyy-mm-dd.

minimum_visits.description: The minimum number of visits to qualify. Default: 1

message.reasoning: The user asks: "How frequent do members at the Museum of Modern Art visi last year?" They want to know how frequent members visited last year. We need to retrieve the visitor who visited the museum the most within a given period. But the question is about frequency of members visits last year. We might interpret as: find the most frequent visitor among members at MoMA last year. Or maybe they want average visits per member? The function most_frequent_visitor returns the visitor who visited the museum the most within a given period. That gives us the top visitor. But the question: "How frequent do members at the Museum of Modern Art visi last year?" It's ambiguous. Could be asking: "How frequent do members visit the Museum of Modern Art last year?" So we need to provide the most frequent visitor among members last year. The function requires museum_name, start_date, end_date. We can set museum_name="Museum of Modern Art", start_date="2023-01-01", end_date="2023-12-31". Minimum_visits default 1. Then call the function.
